answer: Retrospective behavioral echo testing. Each identity's early actions form a private seed; the system later checks whether its later interactions echo that seed too neatly, exposing copied or templated histories. Identities failing a likelihood ratio against a diverse organic garden of genuine behavior are quarantined, forcing attackers to script realistic long-term drift per puppet. An attacker must fund months of varied, non-repeating activity per synthetic ivory identity, so faking N personas costs N times a real user's sustained effort.
